title: Aguinaldo Guyabano (NSIC Ss 02): Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaTitle: Aguinaldo Guyabano: Fruit and Tree Characteristics
metaDescription: Aguinaldo guyabano is a guyabano variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best. Compare it with others.
excerpt: Aguinaldo is a registered guyabano variety, also sold or known as NSIC Ss 02. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2000 as NSIC 2000 Ss 02. Elpidio Panganiban bred it. Its record notes a yield of 20 to 25 fruits.

heroImage.alt: Young fruit trees planted in straight rows on cleared red soil, the kind of farm where Aguinaldo guyabano is grown

blocks.text: If you came here looking for NSIC Ss 02, this is the same guyabano. Its seller and farm sources add notes, listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [guyabano variety finder](/crop-varieties), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for fruit trees](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).

items: **Yield:** a recorded yield of 20 to 25 fruits.

blocks.text: When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. The mother tree of Aguinaldo was about 7 years old and about 15 meters tall when it was registered. Its record notes a yield of 20 to 25 fruits. It bears every year, with fruit in Jan., Mar. and Apr. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit guyabano fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug), [Oriental fruit fly](/pests/oriental-fruit-fly). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.

A fruit of Aguinaldo weighs about 115 grams. The flesh is white and soft. Its sweetness measured 16.5 degrees Brix, the share of sugar in the juice. Most table fruit tastes sweet from about 12 Brix up. The edible part is 77.7 percent of the fruit. Its fruiting season is Jan., Mar. and Apr, bearing annual.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Fruit:** Yellow green smooth skin, soft, juicy white flesh with plenty of fiber, about 16.5 Brix, about 78 percent edible.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: a Cavite guyabano that bears 20 to 25 fruits a year. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Aguinaldo guyabano

Pick a selection with big, evenly shaped fruit and few seeds. Hand pollination helps fruit set. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is NSIC Ss 02 the same as Aguinaldo?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Ss 02 is another name for Aguinaldo, registered as NSIC 2000 Ss 02. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.
The record shows a recorded yield of 20 to 25 fruits. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of Aguinaldo?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
